answer: An agent economy can spot sybils by watching behaviour, not paperwork. Every agent leaves a pulse of actions—timing, ordering, response latency—over weeks. Honest agents drift apart like a meadow of different grasses, while one operator's sockpuppets move in lockstep. The network runs a decorrelation test: identities whose activity correlates above a threshold face a costly interactive task. Faking independence per identity costs real compute and time, so a sable-dark farm of thousands turns uneconomic before it can vote or claim rewards.
